content: 1. Timing of Administration: Administer ceftriaxone 5–2 hours before the procedure. 2. Indications for Uncomplicated Gonococcal Infections: For infections of the pharynx, cervix, urethra, or rectum: If the patient weighs less than 150 kg: Administer ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly (IM) as a single dose. If the patient weighs 150 kg or more: Administer ceftriaxone 1,000 mg IM as a single dose. If chlamydial infection has not been excluded: Add doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 7 days. If the patient is pregnant, administer azithromycin 1,000 mg orally as a single dose. 3. CDC Guidelines for Gonococcal Infections (2020 Update): For toxic shock due to Aeromonas hydrophila: Administer ceftriaxone 1–2 g intravenously (IV) daily in combination with doxycycline. For infections due to Vibrio vulnificus: Administer ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily in combination with doxycycline. Continue treatment until further debridement is unnecessary, clinical improvement is observed, and the patient has been afebrile for 48–72 hours. 4. Hospitalized Infections: Administer ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV every 12–24 hours for 5–7 days. 5. Gonococcal Conjunctivitis: Administer ceftriaxone 1 g IM as a single dose. 6. Disseminated Gonococcal Infection: Administer ceftriaxone 1 g daily (IV or IM) for at least 24–48 hours after clinical improvement, followed by cefixime 400 mg orally every 12 hours to complete at least 1 week of therapy. 7. Gonococcal Endocarditis: Administer ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV every 12 hours for 4 weeks. 8. Gonococcal Meningitis: Administer ceftriaxone 1–2 g IV every 12 hours for 10–14 days. 9. Acute Epididymitis: Administer ceftriaxone 250 mg IM as a single dose in combination with doxycycline. 10. Neonatal Considerations: Ceftriaxone is contraindicated in neonates requiring calcium-containing IV solutions (e.g., parenteral nutrition) due to the risk of precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium complexes, which can be fatal. Separate administration of IV ceftriaxone and calcium-containing solutions by at least 48 hours. 11. Calcium-Containing Solutions: Do not use any calcium-containing solutions (e.g., Ringer’s or Hartmann’s solutions) with IV ceftriaxone due to the risk of potentially fatal particulate precipitation in the lungs and kidneys. Separate administration by at least 48 hours. 12. Drug Interactions: BCG Vaccine (Live): Ceftriaxone decreases the vaccine’s efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. Cholera Vaccine: Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the vaccine within 14 days of antibiotic use. Oral Microbiota: Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Ceftriaxone decreases vaccine efficacy. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. Aminoglycosides (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, tobramycin, streptomycin, neomycin): Ceftriaxone may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use with caution and monitor closely. Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, toripalimab): Coadministration may interfere with therapeutic effects. Use with caution and monitor closely. Tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline): These bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of ceftriaxone, a bactericidal agent. Use with caution and monitor closely. Warfarin: Ceftriaxone may increase the anticoagulant effect. Use with caution and monitor closely. Probenecid: May increase ceftriaxone levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use with caution and monitor closely. Furosemide: Increased risk of nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely. Hormonal Contraceptives (e.g., dienogest/estradiol valerate, bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens): Ceftriaxone may reduce efficacy by altering intestinal flora. Use additional or alternative contraception during concomitant use. Calcium Salts (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate): Contraindicated with IV ceftriaxone due to the risk of precipitation. Separate administration by at least 48 hours. 13. Herbal Interactions: Rose Hips, Willow Bark: May increase ceftriaxone levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Monitor closely.
